pl-l4d3c6-d1e115.summary: Holds that baptism is celebrated only in water, not in any other liquid, as Christ said. It is prescribed uniformly in water so that, as water washes the body and clothes, baptism is understood to cleanse the soul's stains and vices; so that no poverty would excuse anyone, as might happen with wine or oil; and so that a common matter for baptizing would be found among all. The water flowing from Christ's side signified this, as the blood signified the other sacrament.
claims: Baptism can be consecrated only in water.
The water from Christ's side signifies baptism.

pl-l4d3c6.summary: Holds that baptism is celebrated only in water, not in any other liquid, as Christ said 'unless one is reborn of water'. Water was chosen because, as it washes bodies, baptism cleanses the stains of the soul; so that no poverty would excuse anyone, as wine or oil might; so that the matter would be common to all; and as signified by the water from Christ's side, as the blood signified the other sacrament.
claims: Baptism can be performed only in water.
Water signifies cleansing and is available to all.
The water from Christ's side signifies baptism.
